title: The trade-weighted index
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers the trade-weighted index; the closest ones, net trade and the balance of payments, mention currencies or trade flows but never teach how a currency is measured against a weighted basket.

draft.title: The trade-weighted index
card: The Australian dollar can rise against one currency and fall against another. The US dollar rate alone does not show how the dollar is going overall.
The trade-weighted index (TWI) measures the Australian dollar against a basket of the currencies of our trading partners. It gives one number for the dollar's overall value.
Each currency is weighted by how much trade Australia does with that country. A currency of a major trading partner, such as China's, counts for more than one of a small partner.
If the TWI rises, the dollar has risen on average against the basket. If it falls, the dollar has fallen on average. The index is a measure, so it does not set the dollar's value.
draft.remember: The TWI is one average figure for the dollar, with big trading partners counting most.

a.q: Why is the TWI often more useful than the exchange rate with the US dollar alone?
opts: It shows the dollar's average value against many partners
It shows the dollar's value against the most stable currency
It fixes the dollar's value against a basket of currencies
It shows how much Australia has traded with the US
a.why: The TWI combines many currencies into one figure, so it shows the dollar's overall value. The US rate covers only one partner, and the TWI does not fix or set the dollar's value.
a.clue: Think about how many currencies each measure covers.

b.q: The Australian dollar rises against the currency of a small trading partner, but is unchanged against the currencies of its largest partners. What is most likely to happen to the TWI?
opts: It rises by a large amount
b.why: The small partner has a small weight, so its rise lifts the TWI only a little. The TWI would not stay exactly the same, because the rise still counts a little. It would not rise sharply, because the largest partners carry the most weight.
b.clue: Check how much weight a small partner's currency carries.

a.best: It shows the dollar's average value against many partners
